question: What benchmark and evaluation dimensions accompany G-CARL?
answer:
G-CARL is primarily evaluated on the MMedReport dataset [1], which includes subjective and objective evaluation dimensions [1]. Subjective evaluation assesses medical accuracy, demand satisfaction, and expression quality [1]. Objective evaluation reports claim-level Precision and checklist-level Recall [2].

All instances undergo quality control, deidentification,and manualverificationto ensuredataquality andpatientprivacy.Detaileddatasetstatisticsareprovidedin Appendix A. Following the standard split, 2,200 instances areusedfortrainingand250forevaluation.Toassessbroader medical capability beyond PMRI, we further evaluate the trained models on an external benchmark,(2)CMB(Wang et al. 2024), which evaluates both medical QA accuracy and theprofessionalismofopen-endedclinicalinterpretationunder an LLM-as-a-judge protocol. sources.text: QuantitativeComparison.Table1comparesG-CARLwith general-purpose LVLMs, specialized medical LVLMs, and different training paradigms based on the Qwen3-VL and InternVL3 backbones. While the MLLM-as-a-Judge reward improves over SFT, its holistic rubric struggles to jointly optimizemedicalaccuracy,demandsatisfaction,andexpression quality. By decomposing reward supervision into externally verifiable medical claims and internally grounded checklist objectives, G-CARL achieves the highest scores acrossbothobjectiveandsubjectivemetrics.OnQwen3-VL- 8B, G-CARL improves the overall subjective score, while boosting claim-level precision (+0.77%) and checklist-level recall (+6.71%), indicating more informative and richer interpretations. Moreover, G-CARL consistently outperforms specialized medical LVLMs and remains competitive with substantiallylargergeneral-purposeLVLMsunderzero-shot evaluation, demonstrating the effectiveness of G-CARL. External Generalization Study.We further transfer the trained models to CMB without any adaptation. As shown in Table 2, G-CARL improves QA accuracy on both splits (+0.63)andattainsthehighestprofessionalismscoreinopenended generation (3.61), whereas SFT and MLLM-as-a- Judge bring marginal gains and even degrade professionalism. # KPMG Research Executive Brief

## Stakeholder Persona
Allison Tatterson

## Question
What benchmark and evaluation dimensions accompany G-CARL?

## Confidence Tier & Rationale
Moderate (70% evidence score)

Moderate: retrieval scores were not saved and contribute zero. Weights: retrieval 30%, citation coverage 30%, quote/numeric checks 25%, source diversity 15%. This evidence indicator does not verify meaning, answer completeness or business outcomes; human review is required.

## What the Study Found
G-CARL is primarily evaluated on the MMedReport dataset [1], which includes subjective and objective evaluation dimensions [1]. Subjective evaluation assesses medical accuracy, demand satisfaction, and expression quality [1]. Objective evaluation reports claim-level Precision and checklist-level Recall [2].

Evidence:
- "evaluate PMRI responses using both subjective and objective metrics. (1)Subjective Evaluation. Responses are evaluated along three clinician-defined dimensions:Medical Accuracy(Accuracy),Demand Satisfaction(Satisfaction), andExpression Quality(Expression). Each dimension" [1]
- "criteria. The complete judging protocol is provided in theAppendix Bto facilitate reproducibility. (2) Objective Evaluation. In addition to holistic assessment, we report claim-levelPrecisionand checklist-levelRecall." [2]

## Why It Matters to KPMG
Proposed Advisory applications for stakeholder review: Dual supervision of claim factuality and checklist coverage could inform KPMG Trusted AI quality control. [1] The papers do not establish KPMG-specific outcomes or ROI.

## What KPMG Could Consider
Pilot expert-designed case-specific checklists alongside claim verification rather than relying on a single aggregate score; keep domain experts accountable for review.
